features: Number-plate input with a fictional lookup that is deterministic and labelled as a demo
MOT due or overdue counted against the real clock, with the next three free slots on the ramp
Price board as it hangs by the office door, with a Book button on each line that picks the job for you
Half-hour slot booking on a diary built from today, Sundays closed, ending in a booking reference
Real workshop photos, opening hours that say open now or opens at, and a call and book bar on phones
name: Kerb & Camber
short: A UK number plate you type into, and the MOT date that comes back.
long: An independent MOT and service centre where the hero is a real number plate you can type in. Press Check and a job card comes back with the vehicle, the last advisory, how many days until the MOT runs out, and the next three slots on the ramp. Below it sit the price board from the office door, each line with its own Book button, the clock times of a real MOT from keys to away, and a half-hour diary. On a phone the call and book buttons never leave the screen.
proves: Somebody who does not know when their MOT is due can find out and book it before they close the tab.
story: Half the calls a garage takes are somebody asking when their MOT is due. Answering it on the page turns that call into a booking.
